title: AI Valuation Gaps Set to Widen as Investment Cycle Matures
summary:
A volatile month for US equities ended on a higher note Friday, with the S&P 500 Index clocking a 1.1% weekly advance. Much of the comeback can be linked to gains in technology stocks on Thursday and Friday, particularly Microsoft. and Amazon.
Sarah Hunt, Chief Market Strategist at Alpine Saxon Woods, discusses recent tech earnings and their market impact as traders look ahead to jobs data this week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Why Gold Could Reach 5,000
summary: Standard Chartered’s Suki Cooper joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why gold could resume its climb toward 5,000. She says central-bank demand, geopolitical uncertainty, and portfolio diversification remain powerful supports, while recent price resilience suggests gold has established a durable floor despite higher yields and weak ETF positioning. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Whole Foods is Shedding the "Whole Paycheck" Label

title: Yen Rises Amid Speculation of More Intervention After US Support
summary:
The yen rallied sharply on Monday amid speculation that authorities may have intervened to prop up the currency again after coordinated action between the US and Japan last week.
Sonja Marten, Chief Economist at DZ Bank, discusses the global market reaction to the US and Japan taking action on the yen. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tyson Falls on 3Q Results; Bristol-Myers Squibb Surges on Potential Acquisition | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Bristol-Myers Squibb (SQB) shares are surging on news AstraZeneca (AZN), whose shares are lower, is exploring an acquisition of Bristol-Myers Squibb.
- Tyson (TSN) shares are dropping after the protein producer reported a 3Q sales shortfall, driven by a 16% reduction in beef sales volume, and cut its total company and beef profit forecasts for the full year. 
- SpaceX (SPCX) shares are moving as investors in the company prepare for its first earnings report as a public company. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Senators Urge CFTC to Curb Wildfire Prediction Market Bets Over Arson Concerns
summary: A group of Democratic senators urged the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to rein in prediction market trading on wildfires, expressing concern that individuals could be tempted to commit arson to make their bets pay off.

title: Oil Slips as Trump Holds Off Iran Attack, Says Talks to Resume
summary: Oil fell after US President Donald Trump said he called off a planned attack on Iran and that new talks with the Islamic Republic would begin on Monday.

title: Astra Buying Bristol Makes No Sense, Fazeli Says
summary: AstraZeneca shares plunged Monday on news that the drugmaker was exploring an acquisition of Bristol Meyers Squibb. A deal would create one of the world's biggest drugmakers. Sam Fazeli of Bloomberg Intelligence says a takeover would make no sense.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: UBS to Pay $125 Million Over Anti-Money Laundering Violations
summary: UBS Financial Services Inc., a subsidiary of UBS Group AG, has agreed to pay $125 million in fines to settle allegations by the US government that it willfully and repeatedly violated anti-money laundering rules.

title: Blanche Strikes Deal With GOP Senators to Advance Nomination
summary: Two Republican senators are backing a deal with acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to formally rescind an order creating an “anti-weaponization fund,” likely paving the way for Blanche’s confirmation as the nation’s top law enforcement officer. Jeff Mason reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: India Raises Fuel Export Tax to Build Buffer as Wars Curb Supply
summary: India increased levies on exports of oil products to bolster domestic fuel stockpiles while global supplies remained tight despite a pause in fighting between the US and Iran.

title: Citadel Securities Sees a $500 Billion Chip Financing Debt Binge
summary: The credit markets may have had their fill of record borrowing for data centers, but tech companies aren’t done yet. Citadel Securities LLC is forecasting another $500 billion-plus of debt in the public and private markets by 2028 to bankroll the chips that go inside the artificial intelligence campuses.

title: Secular Bull Market Will Last Rest of Decade, Bartels Says
summary: Mary Ann Bartels, Sanctuary Wealth chief investment strategist, says earnings should be celebrated and she says the secular bull market will go out until the end of the decade. She also says the Japanese yen has further to fall. She speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wildfires Fan Record Sales of Catastrophe Bonds to Backstop Risk
summary: Insurers are turning to catastrophe bonds to pass on historic levels of wildfire risk to the capital markets.

title: US Copper Inflows Surge as Market Awaits Trump Tariff Call
summary: Copper is pouring into the US at the fastest rate in at least 12 years as traders position ahead of President Donald Trump’s decision on tariffs on refined imports.
